A witnessed B’s parent commit a homicide and reported it to the authorities. The parent was detained, disrupting the family’s ordinary routine. B or B’s family then chose to transfer B to another school; A’s aim was to report the crime, not to harm B. B did not know about A’s role in the report. They later met at university, began dating, and married.

Years later, B voluntarily disappeared after learning something about A’s past. B had learned that A witnessed the homicide, but that fact itself was not what prompted the disappearance. The answers also connect B’s discovery to an ongoing association A had with someone who had died, but they do not establish precisely what B learned or what specifically prompted B to leave. B remained alive, and A was arrested on suspicion of murdering B, although A had not murdered B.
